takeaways.label: H1 in line, H2 ramp expected
takeaways.text: Q2 revenue grew just 2.9% YoY as seasonal softness and execution phasing compressed the quarter, but H1 revenue rose 10.7% and management is confident in hitting the full-year ₹2,150–2,200 crores target.

takeaways.label: Capex cycle is complete, capacity is live
takeaways.text: Over ₹250 crores deployed across Andhra, Gujarat and Kichha; all new facilities are now operational and the heavy structure plant began contributing only from late September, so the revenue payoff starts in H2.

takeaways.label: Order book crossed ₹2,000 crores
takeaways.text: Heavy structure alone accounts for ₹350–400 crores of that, spanning data centers, a Delhi commercial building, a hospital and a hotel, giving visibility on the new verticals thesis.

takeaways.label: Margins held despite a steel shock
takeaways.text: EBITDA margin slipped only 0.2% YoY to 8.3% even as steel prices hit four-year highs and supply chains broke, a stress-test management used to accelerate the shift to variable-price contracts.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether H2 revenue run-rate reaches the ₹200–220 crores/month needed for the full-year guide, the pace of heavy structure and export order conversion, and any steel price softening that would unlock the promised margin recovery.

points.label: Seasonal H1, loaded H2
points.text: The first half is always softer because monsoons slow execution; Q2 this year was further compressed because Q1 pulled forward more revenue while last year the phasing was reversed, so H1 growth of 10.7% is the better read.

points.label: Inquiry pipeline healthy
points.text: Customer inquiries across key markets remain strong despite the seasonal pattern, giving management confidence in medium-to-long-term demand.

points.label: Order book composition
points.text: Residual order book crossed ₹2,000 crores as of 31st October, representing roughly 9–10 months of production capacity; management says it cannot book beyond its delivery capability.

points.label: Heavy structure loading
points.text: Both heavy structure lines are fully loaded with orders, ~₹350–400 crores of the total book, including a commercial building in Delhi, two data centers, a hospital, a multi-storey hotel, and heavy process buildings for global companies.

points.label: New building types won
points.text: Data centers, hospitals, hotels, a Government of India commercial office building in Delhi, and an airport hangar have all been secured, validating the thesis that steel-frame construction is migrating beyond industrial sheds.

points.label: Business selection tightening
points.text: With abundant demand, management is choosing reliable customers, better pricing, and 100% variable-price contracts to protect against raw-material volatility.

quotes.text: Nanda: "There's a lot of business available in the market, so we are choosing business which is for more reliable customers, better pricing, 100% variable pricing."

points.label: Capex cycle completed
points.text: Interarch has spent over ₹250 crores building the Andhra plant, updating all other plants, adding a line in Kichha, completing a heavy structure plant in Andhra Phase 1, and finishing both phases of the Gujarat plant.

points.label: All facilities now operational
points.text: AP Phase 1 and Gujarat both phases are live and will ramp up quickly in the following quarters; the heavy structure plant came into operation only on 24th September, so its sales contribution begins in Q3 and Q4.

points.label: Heavy structure capacity trajectory
points.text: Currently at 25,000 tons, rising to 75,000–80,000 tons by end of next year; Phase 2 finishes by March/April, Phase 3 by November/December.

points.label: Next expansion leg
points.text: Plan to add another 100,000 tons between March–April '28 and June–July '29, taking total capacity to about 400,000 tons by 2029.

points.label: FY28 usable capacity
points.text: At least 80,000 tons of additional usable capacity from Gujarat Phase 2 and the heavy structure plant, with a goal of 100,000 tons additional salable capacity by March '28.

points.label: Monthly revenue target
points.text: ₹200–220 crores per month over the next 12 months as capacity increases.

quotes.text: Nanda: "In the beginning, it may be a little tight, and we may suffer from expenses because we have to spend money on all these things before we can earn it back. But we don't see any choice for Interarch going forward if you really want to become a steel solutions company to the world and an internationally accepted brand and company."

sections.title: New Verticals: Heavy Structure, Exports & Data Centers

points.label: Three-company structure, one margin
points.text: Management describes Interarch as "working like three different companies" — traditional PEB, heavy structure/data centers, and exports — while "not really earning the margin of even one good company," a candid admission that the investment phase is suppressing returns.

points.label: Heavy structure economics
points.text: Margins are similar to PEB at the gross level, but net margins are expected to be higher because general overhead won't grow proportionately with larger orders; steel prices are always passed through, and payment terms are stricter (no payment after material leaves the factory).

points.label: Export business model
points.text: Design, engineer, manufacture and supply on letter-of-credit basis, carrying no sales cost, no collection cost and no project management cost, which should make it structurally higher-margin once at scale.

points.label: Early export traction
points.text: Orders have been received and will go into execution in Q2 and Q3; strong inroads made into the African continent with a few projects already underway and marketing efforts intensifying.

points.label: OWSJ joint venture
points.text: Building on the MoU with ER Steel Canada to take steel construction solutions to the entire North American market; initial funding of ₹80 crores as planned, and the venture is now formally in place.

points.label: Institutional building pipeline
points.text: Management expects colleges, schools, airports, railway stations and similar institutional buildings to increasingly convert to steel-frame construction, expanding the addressable market beyond industrial and logistics.

points.label: Investment drag is front-loaded
points.text: Significant spending on sales teams, detailing teams, execution teams and production facilities for these two new verticals over the last two years means costs are running ahead of revenue; management expects this to clear up within FY27–28.

points.label: Q2 margin resilience
points.text: EBITDA margin declined only 0.2% YoY (8.5% to 8.3%) despite steel prices at four-year highs, supply disruptions forcing purchases from traders at a premium, and unusual oil and freight cost volatility.

points.label: What compressed PAT
points.text: Q2 PAT fell to ₹30.7 crores from ₹32.3 crores YoY because of higher depreciation from capitalizing two new facilities (Gujarat and AP) and lower interest income as cash was deployed into capex.

points.label: Erection and installation costs
points.text: Rose from 9% to 11% of top-line YoY because larger jobs and jobs in remote locations cost more in erection and freight, but these are fully pass-through costs charged to the customer, not absorbed by Interarch.

points.label: New vertical cost overhang
points.text: Exports and heavy-structure building sales added heavily to design engineering, traveling and selling costs in H1, disproportionately to sales because turnover from these orders comes in later quarters.

points.label: Working capital stretched
points.text: Gross working capital days rose from 66 to 86 days because of longer execution cycles on larger orders with bill certification processes, erratic steel supply chains forcing higher inventory stocking, steel price increases, and two new plants becoming operational requiring critical mass of inventory; net working capital remains at 44 days after customer advances.

points.label: FY27 margin outlook
points.text: Not expecting much improvement for the full year; H2 may improve from operating leverage on higher turnover (₹1,200 crores in H2 vs ₹950 crores in H1) but not expected to cross 9% to 9.5%.

points.label: FY28 margin catalyst
points.text: Better margins expected as full capacity of Gujarat, full capacity of the heavy structure plant, and export deliveries all contribute simultaneously.

quotes.text: Nanda: "We are not happy at all. I mean, currently EBITDA is about 9% or something, 8.5%. I don't think that is the kind of EBITDA we deserve as a company."

points.label: Unprecedented steel environment
points.text: Steel prices behaved in a way not seen for four to five years; normally they fall during monsoon but this time they rose, and steel companies prioritized exports for better realization, disrupting domestic supply.

points.label: Supply-chain response
points.text: Interarch was forced to hold higher stocks and sometimes buy from traders and dealers at a premium to avoid project delays, compressing margins on fixed-price orders bid earlier.

points.label: Order-book pricing mix
points.text: Currently 35–40% variable-price orders and 60% fixed-price, but the blended approach and dynamic pricing system protected EBITDA at 8.4% despite erratic raw material increases.

points.label: Aggressive shift to variable pricing
points.text: Over the last five to six months, the company has been moving very fast toward variable pricing; in the last two to three months, probably no order was taken at fixed price because steel prices are at four-year highs and the direction is uncertain.

points.label: Policy going forward
points.text: In the next couple of quarters, management will not change the policy of refusing fixed-price contracts; longer-term orders like data centers and heavy structure are traditionally all pass-through or variable anyway, so the variable proportion will keep increasing.

points.label: Steel price outlook
points.text: Management expects stabilization or softening in the next few months, which should improve profitability.

points.label: Bid-to-execution mismatch
points.text: Orders executed in Q3 and Q4 were generally bid in Q1 and Q2 when steel prices were already higher, and those bids were based on anticipated price cycles from Q3 and Q4 of the prior year, so margin took a hit from that timing gap.

quotes.text: Nanda: "The way steel prices have behaved this year, we have not seen them behave like this for last four or five years."

points.label: Leadership transition
points.text: Arvind Nanda newly appointed as Executive Chairman; Manish Garg newly appointed as MD and CEO, formalizing a succession that puts operational leadership in place for the next growth phase.

points.label: QIP ready to launch
points.text: All legal formalities have been completed; the issue can launch at 72-hour notice once merchant banker Ambit decides the right timing; management wants it done sooner rather than later since expansion plans are at full speed, but declined to give a specific timeline when pressed.

points.label: Government tailwind
points.text: The government has released the draft 2047 Steel Policy, anticipating steel usage to go up many notches, which supports the thesis of structural conversion to steel-frame construction across building types.

quotes.text: Nanda: "It's like managing a lot of balls. You've got a lot of balls up in the air and now you have to manage to juggle them properly. Some will fall down, but otherwise as a business it is our job."

items.title: FY28 revenue guide ₹2,700 crore
items.text: Management raised its FY28 projection to ₹2,700 crore including ₹200 crore from heavy structures, up from ₹2,500 crore earlier, after reaffirming FY27 guidance of ₹2,150 crore. Against FY26 revenue of ₹1,898 crore, that implies roughly ₹800 crore of added turnover over two years, with EBITDA margins guided to 10-12% over the next 12 months as Gujarat, heavy structures and exports ramp.

items.title: Heavy steel structures ramp at Athivaram
items.text: Phase 1 (25,000 MTPA) of the Andhra Pradesh HSS plant started commercial production on 24 September 2026, lifting total capacity to 245,000 MT, with Phase 2 due Q4 FY27 and all three phases accelerated to complete within 1.5 years for 75,000-80,000 tons of HSS capacity. HSS revenue was already ₹209 crore in H1 FY27 versus ₹72 crore a year earlier - nearly 3x - and cumulative orders exceed 1 lakh tons, with the segment opening data-center, high-rise and semiconductor work previously out of reach.

items.title: Gujarat capacity build-out
items.text: Phase 2 at Kheda (20,000 MT) commenced commercial production on 5 November 2026, taking installed capacity to 265,000 MT just four months after Phase 1 started in July, funded from internal accruals at just ₹75 crore combined. Land for a sixth ~40,000-ton plant was registered on 24 March 2026 for ₹50-60 crore of capex, targeting production by Q1 FY28 and lifting peak revenue capacity to ~₹3,000 crore.

items.title: ER Steel JV for North American exports
items.text: The Board approved the definitive joint venture agreement on 6 August 2026 (76% Interarch), with ER Steel contractually bound to a 100% offtake of the output for Canada and the USA; a 15,000-tonne plant at Athivaram should see first production around July 2027, with the first 4,000-5,000-tonne phase worth ~₹70-75 crore at ~20% EBITDA margin. The near-term plan is 2-5% North American market share in three years, and management projects the OWSJ/exports stream doubling from ~₹200 crore (FY28-29) to ~₹400 crore (FY29-30).

items.title: Export orders scaling toward 10% of revenue
items.text: Management is targeting at least ₹100 crore of export orders in FY27 (₹30-35 crore already in hand, after FY26's ₹40.2 crore from Canada, Kenya, Myanmar and Ghana), with a 1-2 year goal of ~10% of turnover from exports versus ~3-3.5% today. US welding/fabrication certifications and Canadian market approvals are complete, and export contracts are supply-only with LC or advance backing, carrying higher margins and faster working-capital cycles than domestic orders.

items.title: ₹250 crore QIP to fund the pipeline
items.text: The QIP was upsized from ₹100 crore to ₹250 crore on 6 August 2026, earmarked for heavy-structure Phases 2-3 (₹150 crore), Gujarat Plant 2 (₹50-60 crore) and the open-web-joist export unit (₹50-60 crore), with legal formalities done and launch possible at 72-hour notice. Nearly debt-free (D/E 0.01), the company can complete the +1,24,600 MT pipeline to ~3,70,600 MT by FY29 without straining the balance sheet.
